item.title: [github_trending] pbakaus/impeccable

item.title: [infoq] 谷歌赢了 AI 排行榜，却没赢下华尔街：Gemini 4 Carbon 登顶背后的昂贵代价
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28, roughly two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon opened to wider users. It tops Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index v5.0 with 59 points, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 and GPT-6 Astra at 57, and ranks second on the Coding Agent Index, three points behind Opus 5.5. Built for long-running agentic work and vulnerability discovery, it is first limited to vetted security defenders, with access widening later through the Fairwind program.

item.description: A developer working at a foreign company built Inklet, a Mac menu bar app: press ⌥ Space in any text field, type in Chinese, hit enter and natural English is generated and filled back into the box. It is MIT-licensed, needs no API key, runs local models offline on M-series Macs, and also supports DeepSeek, Claude, OpenAI and Gemini, plus local voice input and selected-text translation. Requires macOS 14+, and the build is signed and notarized.

item.title: [infoq] Anthropic 取消编程面试：新人第一次有机会直接和资深工程师竞争

He also argues "hunger beats tenure": newcomers unburdened by assumptions about what can't be done can use AI to catch up fast.

item.description: Local-AI-Route is a process-level local proxy launcher and manager for desktop AI apps, routing traffic per process without a global TUN interface or changes to system proxy settings. item.title: [infoq] Uber 实现服务网格依赖关系分析自动化
item.description: Uber detailed how it automates service-mesh dependency mapping: YARPC inbound and outbound middleware generate a request ID, propagate it through Go's context, and log caller and downstream endpoint outcomes in an in-memory RequestTracker. Dependencies are then labeled fail-close (correlation ≥0.8), fail-open (≤0.2) or unknown. Uber skipped distributed tracing because rare failures sample too slowly — at 99.9% availability and a 0.01% sampling rate, catching a failed request could take hours.

item.description: A Chinese engineering post breaks down a question now common in 2026 interviews, including the variant "if I gave you an intern plus Claude Code, could they replace you?", and explains why stock answers such as "AI code quality is bad" no longer land. The author's own answer has two layers: AI writes code while humans make decisions, and AI writes one file while humans design a system, illustrated by an e-commerce countdown component whose edge cases the model never raises on its own.
